messages:
Leila: hey team, new here. i'm prepping a short product demo and opening 6 browser-based streaming clients. i'm already seeing 429s. is that just sandbox being small or am i doing something wrong?
Tom: welcome! sandbox is shared and conservative by default. 6 concurrent streams can definitely trigger the concurrent-streams or requests/sec bucket.
Leila: how can i tell which bucket is the culprit? the client just shows 429.
Grace: check the 429 response headers and body. we include remaining, reset, and a reason string. sample: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1876543250
x-rw-retry-after: 2.0
{ "error":"rate_limited", "reason":"concurrent_streams" }
```
Tom: if reason == "tokens_per_min" you'll know it's token budget. embeddings sometimes have separate counters (look for x-rw-embed-* headers).
Leila: nice. can devex grant a short bump for a live demo?
DevExBot: to request a temporary boost, post in #devex with your email, demo window, and approximate concurrent connections. quick boosts for new hires are usually 24248h. creating a ticket now.
Infra: operational tip: instead of launching N separate real streams, multiplex many logical sessions over one socket or reuse one long-lived connection. that avoids hitting connection caps.
Leila: any quick code pattern references for multiplexing?
Grace: simple pattern: open one websocket, tag each message with a session_id, and route server-side. keeps client counts low. also trim prompt histories and cap max_tokens to reduce tokens/min consumption.
Tom: add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s (e.g., base 300ms, cap 4s). for demos, you can also simulate parallel users by replaying prerecorded outputs for non-present tabs.
Leila: thanks. i'm going to request the demo boost and try multiplexing first. pinging #devex now.
DevExBot: ticket DX-9832 created for Leila (sandbox boost requested, 24h).
Leila: perfect, appreciate it! :raised_hands:
